english.title: Immigration - unlawful disclosure of information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[an Immigration Services Commissioner appointed pursuant to Part V of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999]_
(B)_[a member of the staff of the Immigration Services Commissioner]_
(C)_[an agent of the Immigration Services Commissioner]_

knowingly or recklessly and without lawful authority, disclosed information, namely **(..SPECIFY..), which had been obtained by, or given to, the Commissioner under or for the purposes of this Act, and related to an identified or identifiable individual or business which was not at the time, and had not previously been, available to the public from other sources
english.legislation: Contrary to section 93(2) and (4) of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999.

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes: See Section 93(3) for conditions under which disclosure can lawfully be made.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
